column1: # Spanish diacritic-fold table (D-436) - base letter -> every real accented variant, so a token typed
# without its accent ("nino") still reaches the correctly-spelled word ("niño"), both live while typing
# and at autocorrect/split-repair time. hints.tsv (same folder) picks one representative symbol per key
# for the AltGr long-press hint; this file keeps the complete set per base letter. "n" is included too:
# n is spelled without a tilde only via a typo, never a genuine alternate ASCII convention the way German
# ss/ß has two legitimate spellings - but the tilde-to-base-letter relationship is otherwise the same
# shape D-436's DataDiacriticFolding already handles generically (one base letter, one real ASCII
# substitution), so a dedicated hardcoded special case like German's own Umlaut object is not needed here.
